The setup concerns Drinfeld cusp forms at $\wp$-power level. For a Hecke eigensystem $\lambda$ of finite $\wp$-slope occurring in $S_k(\Gamma_1(\mathfrak{n}\wp))$, the growth of its multiplicity when the level is raised from $\Gamma_1(\mathfrak{n}\wp)$ to $\Gamma_1(\mathfrak{n}\wp^r)$ is governed by the local structure at $\wp$.

The finite slope condition ensures that the local component at $\wp$ behaves like a ramified principal series-type representation (the $U_\wp$-operator acts invertibly), and the space of invariants under the higher congruence subgroup $K_1(\wp^r)$ grows by a factor equal to the $(r-1)$-st power of the cardinality of the residue field at $\wp$. Since $\wp$ has degree $D$, the residue field $\mathbb{F}_q[t]/(\wp)$ has $q^D$ elements. Consequently, each copy of $\lambda$ at level $\Gamma_1(\mathfrak{n}\wp)$ spawns exactly $q^{D(r-1)}$ independent copies at level $\Gamma_1(\mathfrak{n}\wp^r)$.

Thus the ratio of multiplicities is:
\[
\frac{\dim S_k(\Gamma_1(\mathfrak{n}\wp^r))[\lambda]}{\dim S_k(\Gamma_1(\mathfrak{n}\wp))[\lambda]} \;=\; q^{D(r-1)}.
\]

\boxed{q^{D(r-1)}}
